author: ABQ Times
title: Bernalillo County approves $6.3 million for 4th Street Road Diet Project
text:
The Bernalillo County Board of Commissioners approved the 4th Street Road Diet Project on Mar. 24, allocating $6.3 million for roadway, drainage, and pedestrian safety improvements between Ortega Road and Alameda Boulevard in District 4.
The project is intended to enhance transportation infrastructure and improve safety for drivers and pedestrians in the area. It will be managed by Commissioner Walt Benson’s district.
Compass Engineering was selected as the lowest bidder after bids were advertised in January. The funding comes from the county’s Biennial Budget and Road Bonds, according to county officials. Construction is set to begin this summer and continue through winter of 2027, with regular updates planned for residents regarding any delays or road closures during construction.
Meanwhile, concerns about public safety remain prominent in Bernalillo County. The District Attorney has voiced frustration over suspects being released without GPS monitors when they are supposed to have one according to KRQE News. In a recent case highlighted by local media, Jawid Yaqubi was accused of aggravated assault involving a firearm at his family home but was released pending trial despite efforts by the DA’s office to keep him in custody.
County officials say they will keep residents informed as construction progresses on the road project.
